purpose: The trusted half of the foreign-voice gate (design 3.1). Each row maps one
constructor of the FOREIGN DIALECT -- a binder, a connective, a relation, an
operator, a type name or a grouping mark -- to one English word phrase.
Forward it lexicalizes; reversed it de-lexicalizes. It is not an independent
check and is not claimed as one: its correctness is carried by review,
exactly as data/realization/lexicon.json's rows are. The independent check
is the PINNED EXTERNAL LEAN CHECKER, which this repository did not build and
which has never seen this table.
It inherits v0.18's lexicon rules WHOLE rather than restating them:
what make stage one 'a table lookup with no lookahead policy of its own'.
what_is_rendered: THE RENDERER RENDERS R(s), NOT s. Correction 3 of the design is why: with
autoImplicit off -- and it must be off -- the surface handed to the oracle
has to carry an explicit binder preamble, so the sentence a reader sees is
the sentence for the statement UNDER THE DECLARED INTERPRETATION. Every
receipt carries `interpretation_shift` naming each substitution rule R
applied. A rate quoted without that field beside it is a number pretending
reading_rules: LONGEST MATCH: reading a surface left to right, take the longest phrase in
this table that matches the upcoming words; if none matches, expect a
numeral run (scripts/numeral_words). The loader makes longest match the
UNIQUE match by enforcing two properties, so the inverter needs no lookahead
policy of its own:
L1 prefix-free -- no phrase is a proper word-prefix of another phrase;
L2 numeral-disjoint -- no phrase word is a word the registered numeral
pair can emit, so one word decides numeral-run versus phrase and a
numeral run may be scanned greedily.
SLOT MARKER: the word `variable` is followed by a numeral run giving the
slot's index; the pair emits the token v<index>. Identifiers are erased to
indices ON PURPOSE and this is the one place the design's own prerequisite
pays for itself: Serialize.lean drops the `Name` field of every forallE, lam
and letE, so binder names are invisible to the identity witness by
CONSTRUCTION. Rendering a name would put information in the sentence that
the gate cannot see, which is the shape of a rendering error B1 could never
catch. The source's own identifiers are carried in the receipt's
`parameters.surface_slot_names` instead. Indices are assigned by first
occurrence in R(s), left to right.
TOKENS ARE SPACE-SEPARATED ON THE WAY BACK. The inverse writes each token
with a single space around it, so the pinned binary's lexer never has to
decide a maximal munch this table could have got wrong. `- 5` and `-5` are
the same term to Lean; `v1 0` and `v10` are not, which is exactly why the
separation is a rule and not a convenience.
NUMERALS ARE UNSIGNED. `-` is always the operator row, never part of a
literal, so the numeral pair is only ever asked for non-negative values and
its word `negative` never appears in a foreign-voice surface. This is what
removes v0.18's neg/sub collision at the root instead of legislating around
it: there is exactly one `-` row and it emits exactly one token.
PRECEDENCE IS CARRIED, NOT REBUILT. The rendering keeps R(s)'s own
parentheses as `the quantity` / `end quantity` rows and adds none, because
the inverse feeds the result back to the SAME grammar it came from -- Lean's
-- so the source's bracketing is already exactly the bracketing the reader
needs. This is narrower than v0.18's realizer, which had to re-bracket for a
different grammar, and the narrowing is stated rather than discovered: a
renderer that added minimal brackets here would be adding surface outside
this table.
NO ROW IS IMPROVISED. A dialect construct with no row REFUSES AT THE
SURFACE, with a reason from `refusal_reasons`, and the statement lands in
the frozen register instead of in a rendering.
refusal_reasons_note: A closed vocabulary, in the spirit of v0.18's nine reasons
`interpretation_absent` are decided before rendering; the other three are
decided by this table and the registered numeral pair.

why: An up-arrow is a request to insert a coercion whose target type the
elaborator chooses. Rendering it as a word would put a phrase in the
sentence whose meaning depends on an elaboration decision the reader
cannot see, and inverting that phrase would name a coercion this table
cannot commit to. Measured on the eligible set: 9 occurrences across 4
statements. They are registered, not rendered.

naming_conventions: Every phrase is lowercase ASCII words separated by single spaces.
The connectives read as sentence glue rather than as symbol names -- `and
also`, `or else`, `implies that`, `exactly when`, `it fails that` -- because
the surface has to be one readable sentence for C-V3's determinacy sheet to
be answerable at all, and because a phrase like `logical and` would put the
word `and` in a position where L1 has to work harder than it needs to.
The two binder phrases share a first word (`for every` / `for some`) and the
two `it ...` connectives share theirs; both pairs differ at the second word,
so L1 holds with room to spare. This is checked by the loader, not by the
`divided by` rather than `over`, and `minus` rather than `negative`, because
`over` and `negative` are both words the registered numeral pair emits and
L2 would refuse the table at load. The gate caught both spellings during
authoring, which is the gate working.

constructive_check: Every one of the 2,319 oracle-eligible statements was tokenized under R
with exactly this table's tokens, the identifier grammar of rule_r.json
and the registered numeral pair. Leftover characters: ONE -- the coercion
arrow, 9 occurrences across 4 statements, which has a refusal row above.
Nothing else in the eligible set is outside this table.
This is the whole-table check v0.18's `head_coverage` block does for the
realization lexicon, done constructively rather than by head census,
because this dialect's vocabulary is closed and small enough to enumerate

identifiers.note: All opaque variable names, all erased to `variable <index>` by the slot marker; none of them needs a row.

note: One lean_workbook statement carries a 433-digit integer, which is outside
scripts/numeral_words' registered domain (abs < 10^15) and refuses as
whose canonical decimal spellings are `23.5` and `39.5`; the numeral
pair is exact rather than approximately exact, so it cannot reproduce a
trailing zero, and `23.50` and `23.5` are DIFFERENT `OfScientific`
terms to the elaborator. That statement refuses as
`noncanonical_numeral` rather than round-tripping to a term the corpus
did not write. Both are register entries.
